text: dsh-hashline-edittool 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的代码编辑插件，通过 DSH 工具层接入内容锚点式 read、edit、write 和 grep，并提供文件删除、重命名、撤销、结构化搜索与格式化。它还接入 AST 结构操作和可选语言服务器能力，让代码行可以用锚点引用，并将搜索或语义定位结果用于后续编辑。Web 客户端可呈现读取、差异、搜索及设置卡片。适合希望在 DSH 中直接查看、修改和理解项目代码的开发者；需要兼容版本的 Node.js 与 DSH 文件系统服务。

dsh-hashline-edittool adds anchored code reading and editing, text and AST search, undo, rename, and formatting to DSH. Its language-server tool finds definitions, references, and diagnostics. Search results can feed into edits. The web client renders code cards.
我想让代码编辑按读到的行标记定位，避免重复粘贴整段旧代码。
有没有办法在 DSH 里搜索文件内容并直接拿搜索结果继续编辑？
我需要按语法结构查找代码，而不是误匹配注释和字符串。
想在 DSH 中查看符号定义、引用和诊断信息。
我希望对项目文件做格式化、删除或重命名操作。
编辑代码后发现改错了，想撤销最近一次修改。
I want code edits to target lines I have read without pasting the old text again.
Can I search source files and reuse the matching lines in an edit?
dsh-hashline-edittool 的功能「锚点读写」：read 展示带内容锚点的文件行，edit 使用这些锚点批量替换、插入或删除行，write 提供文件写入预览。
dsh-hashline-edittool 的功能「代码搜索与语义导航」：grep 查找文本，ast_grep 按语法模式查找结构；lsp 可查询定义、引用、符号、悬停信息和诊断。
dsh-hashline-edittool 的功能「项目文件操作」：提供删除、重命名、格式化及撤销最近编辑的工具；格式化工具可针对文件或指定锚点范围操作。

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Introduction：

dsh-hashline-edittool README · What it is：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) plugin that replaces the built-in
`read` / `edit` / `grep` tools with **hash-anchored** versions and adds `delete`, `rename`,
`undo_last_edit`, `ast_grep`, `ast_edit`, `apply_patch`, and an `lsp` tool on top:

dsh-hashline-edittool README · What it is：- **Every line carries a content anchor** — a variable-length Base62 marker (2 characters
  covers the first 3,844 lines; the encoding grows only as the file demands). The model
  edits by marker, so it never echoes the code it is replacing.
- **Edits are verified against what the model actually saw.** Each referenced anchor is
  checked line by line: it must still be live, its line must still hold the content it
  was minted for, and it must be in *this session's* served set **as the binding the session saw** — an anchor another session released and re-minted onto different content carries a different fingerprint and fails here. A line that changed
  under the agent is refused — and the refusal echoes the failing lines **with real,
  immediately usable anchors** (reject-and-serve). A changed file checksum is a *remap*
  signal, not a refusal, so another session touching another line never invalidates yours.
- **Anchors are shared across sessions in one workspace.** Read a file in one session and
  edit it from another without re-reading: anchors are a per-workspace identity, while
  "may I write this line" is answered per session. If the o

dsh-hashline-edittool README · What it is：Ships as one npm package (`dsh-hashline-edittool`): host plugin + web card plugin + prompt
sections, mounted by a single bundle patch.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Self-rendering cards.** The bundled client plugin ships its own React components —
`HashlineReadRow`, `HashlineEditRow`, `HashlineGrepRow` (file tabs + match highlighting),
`HashlineUndoRow`, `HashlineWriteRow`, `HashlineAstGrepRow`, `HashlineAstEditRow`,
`HashlineLspRow` — registered straight into the dsh web UI's slots. Every card renders
from the tool's structured `presentationMeta`, with anchor gutters, diff rows, and
highlight spans drawn natively. No generic tool-output cards, no string parsing, no
upstream web changes.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Card chrome follows the reader.** The five card kinds (read / grep / diff / LSP /
error) wrap by default, and a button in the card title switches a card back to
horizontal scrolling (#373). The card text follows the DSH interface language (zh/en;
any other language falls back to English): the wording lives in the plugin's own
`hashline.card` vocabulary, and the host sends stable keys over the wire instead
of prose (#372, #375).

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Dynamic-length anchors.** Anchors are not fixed-width hashes. Allocation is
shortest-first: 2 characters cover the first 3,844 lines, and a new layer grows only when
the file demands it (up to 62⁸ lines — practically unbounded). All-digit encodings are
skipped so a marker can never be confused with a line number, collisions are probed and
resolved at allocation time, and surviving lines keep their anchors across edits within
the session.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**AST + LSP, two semantic backends.** `ast_grep` / `ast_edit` answer "where does the
syntax match" through a sandboxed tree-sitter worker, with a curated grammar catalog
(SHA-256-pinned downloads, install/uninstall routes) and folded editable outlines for
long files. The `lsp` tool answers "what does this symbol mean" through a real language
server per language — started on demand, shared with dsh's own `lsp` service — and falls
back to a heuristic backend when none can be had. Both serve their rows, so structural and
semantic results are directly editable. A server nobody is using is reclaimed after
`lsp.idle_timeout_ms` (five minutes by default) and warmed again on the next use — a
TypeScript server holding a large repository's index is not something to keep
resident for the whole session. A server that fails to start retries on the next use once its backoff window passes (5 s doubling, capped at 1 min; the counter resets on success), `lsp { operation: "warm", language }` forces an immediate restart past the backoff, and `status` reports every started language's server state without starting anything (#318).

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Diagnostics on write.** After an edit/write lands, the plugin baselines the language server with the pre-write text, pulls diagnostics, and delivers them per written file — an inline, severity-tinted capsule under the card within a short window, with bounded async delivery at the model's next natural step, riding both the JSON envelope and the text channel. One switch (`lsp.auto_diagnostics`) turns it off.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Formatting through the language server.** The `format` tool asks the server's formatter to do the work — with indentation read from the project's `.editorconfig` when present (`format.editorconfig`, on by default) and otherwise inferred from the file's own indent **steps** (a deep 4-space file stays 4-space; #336). `format.auto` is a three-way switch (#315): **off** (default) never formats behind the tools' backs, **full** formats the whole file after every content-changing `write`/`edit`/`ast_edit`, and **range** formats only the lines the call touched — falling back to whole-file only when the server lacks range formatting AND `format.fallback_full_file` is on (otherwise the pass is skipped silently, and the `format` tool with an explicit range refuses with `E_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED` instead of guessing). Ready servers only (never started for this), a 2 s budget per file, one warning + a skipped section when a request fails. The card shows the formatter's extra changes as their own section under the diff — header first (`[auto-format: server · mode · requested → applied · n lines changed · k in main diff · r restored · u unserved]`) — and n

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Write preview.** `write`'s post-write echo is the user's call (`write.preview`, map #354). **diff** (default) renders an overwrite as the same unified diff every edit tool uses — `--- path` / `+++ path`, the `@@ … @@ scope()` header, `context_lines` of context, and `+`/`-` rows whose `+` and context anchors are editable immediately; a create has no before side, so it stays read-style. **full** keeps the whole-file auto-read preview. **confirmation** returns one line (`Wrote <path> (update).`) and serves nothing: no file window, no resume token, no anchors — the card still draws the diff, but its gutter carries line numbers only. JSON output follows the same choice: `diff` answers with the marker-keyed diff dictionary `edit` uses, `confirmation` with `{path, operation}`.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**A settings panel rendered by the plugin itself.** The bundled `HashlineSettingsCard` is
a full settings UI in the web: separator, output format, context lines, line numbers
(the model-facing marker shape — the user's call, not the agent's), require_line_content,
the AST master switch plus per-language toggles, named LSP servers, auto-diagnostics,
the language server's idle-reclaim window.
Edit, commit, done — no YAML editing required.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Highlights：**Hot switching, everywhere.** A committed settings change takes effect on the **next
tool call** — output format, separator, context lines, AST/LSP toggles (verified live:
flipping `output_format` mid-session immediately changes what the model receives). And the
switch with the biggest blast radius is handled too: flipping `require_line_content`
disposes and re-registers the `edit` tool's schema, so the model's very next step sees the
new `{ anchor, line }` parameter set — no restart anywhere.

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-hashline-edittool                       # from npm
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-hashline-edittool              # local checkout

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Markers：- An anchor is a variable-length Base62 marker, **unique per line** (identical content
  lines get *distinct* anchors — the anchor is a row identity, not a content hash you can
  guess). Digits-only encodings are skipped, so a marker is never all digits.
- A marker is written `<anchor>` or `<anchor>:<line>`; `line` is a **positional hint only**
  — the anchor is authoritative, and a disagreeing hint is a warning
  (`[E_LINE_HINT]`), not an error. The legacy `<line>:<anchor>` order is still accepted.
- `read` output opens with an `ANCHOR:FILELINE` header separating the marker column from
  verbatim content, using the configured separator (`|` in the examples below):

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Edit diffs (unified diff)：Every edit answers with a **unified diff** — file header, segment headers, then the
rows — not a floating list of changed lines:

```text
Diff rows: <+|-><anchor>:<content> — a unified diff: `@@ -old,count +new,count @@ scope()` gives the line range and the enclosing function(s); `-` rows are the pre-edit lines (their `~` anchors are stale), `+` rows and unchanged rows are the post-edit code.
--- src/render/line-diff.ts
+++ src/render/line-diff.ts
@@ -194,7 +194,7 @@ myersRange()

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Edit diffs (unified diff)：- `--- path` / `+++ path` — the file. A multi-file edit prints one group per file.
- `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@ scope()` — one **segment**: the line range before and after the edit (context lines counted, git convention) plus the enclosing function or class — every scope the segment's changes fall into, joined by ` / ` when one segment touches more than one. The language is chosen by file extension or name (TS/JS, Vue/Svelte, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust, Zig, Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, Swift, the C family, Dart, Groovy, Solidity, PHP, Perl, Shell, PowerShell, Lua, Elixir, Julia — the same way git picks its pattern table, and table-driven so a new language is one row). The name is information only — a file whose scope cannot be detected simply has no name.
- `-` rows are the **pre-edit** lines. Their anchor is stale and carries a `~`, so a model that copies it gets a clean `[E_BAD_REF]` instead of a rescued-then-stale anchor.
- `+` and unchanged rows are the **post-edit** code, and their anchors are fresh and editable.
- How much of the file a segment covers follows `hashline.context_lines`: raise it to see more of

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：A row becomes **served** when a tool result shows it to the model (`read`, `grep`, edit
diffs, structural results, LSP rows). Anchors are minted at exactly that moment, through
**one** entry point, and the mint and the served record commit together — an anchor the
model was shown is always an anchor some session has "seen", which is what the
verification below relies on.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：**Allocation happens after the response is truncated.** A line cut by the response budget
is a line the model never saw, so it is neither anchored nor served; it gets its anchor
when a later call actually shows it. "I hold a marker" therefore always means "I have
seen that line".

`edit` verifies each referenced anchor **line by line**, against three conditions — all
of which must hold:

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：**A changed file checksum is not itself a rejection.** It is the signal that the file was
changed by something else, and it triggers a **remap**: unchanged lines keep their
anchors at their new line numbers, and only lines whose content actually changed are
released and re-minted. Refusing on the checksum would make a line uneditable the moment
someone else touched any other part of the file — which is exactly what cross-session
anchors exist to avoid.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：**Releasing an anchor clears three things together**: the anchor stops being live, it
leaves the *releasing* session's served set, and it enters that call's release pool so the
same call cannot hand it to a different line. Anything less leaves the silent
wrong-line window: an anchor that resolves, verifies and points somewhere new.

Failure is **all-or-nothing** and the code is unchanged:

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：- anchor unknown → `[E_STALE]`; a range row never served in this session → `[E_RANGE_UNVERIFIED]`;
- `[E_RANGE_STALE]` for a changed file checksum (a remap signal, not a refusal) and for a **rebound** binding (#420): the session saw this anchor under different content — another session released and re-minted it — so the content now under it has never been read. The host's
  own `FS_STALE_VERSION` (the write was refused by the file-version guard) maps onto the same code
  because the remedy is the same — re-read for fresh anchors;
- every rejection **echoes the failing lines with a little context, as served rows with
  real anchors**, so the fix is: take the marker from the echo and resubmit. Served rows
  are also emitted as `fs/observed`, so they can be written with immediately.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Served-state verification (reject-and-serve)：There is no `Shift:` block — after an edit, take anchors from the diff rows the response
just gave you, or re-read.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Batch semantics：- `edits[]` apply **in order against one snapshot**; overlapping ranges are
  `[E_BATCH_CONFLICT]`; any failure in that file's batch is `[E_BATCH_ABORT]` and that file is
  left untouched.
- With per-item `path` (or every item carrying `path`), items are grouped per file and each
  file is **all-or-nothing independently**; results aggregate as `success[]` / `fail[]`
  (multi-file form). `item.path === topLevelPath` is auto-folded to absent.
- **Partial failure is visible**: when at least one file succeeds and another fails, the call is
  *not* a failure — every failed file is reported with its own code and recovery hint, and the web
  card draws a `N of M files failed` banner plus one tab per failed file (marked in the tab strip).
  The aggregate `[E_BATCH_ABORT]` message, and its "nothing was written", belongs to calls where
  **every** file failed.
- No cap on the number of edits per call — each edit addresses its own line, so a batch is only as long as the change.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · `op` semantics：| op | anchor field | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replace` | `anchor_start` (+ optional `anchor_end`) | swap the range for `lines` (non-empty; **one element = one line** — only an element's own newline adds a line; `[""]` clears a line to empty, distinct from `del`). `anchor_end` omitted = single-line replace; **required when the range spans multiple lines**. |
| `ins` | `anchor_after` | insert `lines` **below** that line — the anchor line is kept, `lines` holds only what is new. `anchor_start`/`anchor_end` are refused. May anchor on another hunk's range **end** line, never its start/interior. A pasted row (`<anchor>:<content>`) is salvaged to its anchor with an `[E_BAD_REF]` warning — the anchor line is never replaced. |
| `del` | `anchor_start` (+ optional `anchor_end`) | delete the range (or the single `anchor_start` line); `lines` is ignored. |
| `sed` | `anchor_start` (+ optional `anchor_end`) | rewrite the range **line by line** with `pattern` + `replacement` + optional `flags` (`gims`), no `lines`, no newline in `replacement`; sed's `\1`/`&` and JS's `$1`/`$&` both accepted. |
dsh-hashline-edittool README · `op` semantics：Mixing anchor fields with the wrong op is `[E_BAD_SHAPE]`.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · `require_line_content` (optional hardening)：When `hashline.require_line_content` is on, every anchor becomes a
`{ anchor, line }` pair — `line` is your declaration of that row's **current full text**.
Declarations are verified after the stale-anchor check; a mismatch rejects that file's batch with
`[E_CONTENT_MISMATCH]` and echoes where your declared content actually lives.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · `grep_respect_gitignore` (default on)：`grep` builds its candidate list with ripgrep, so `.gitignore` / `.ignore` rules decide what
is searched at all: build output and vendored copies never reach the read stage (nor its
64 MiB budget). Only the **searched tree's own** ignore files apply — naming an ignored
directory on purpose still searches it. Turn `hashline.grep_respect_gitignore` off to
search what the plugin's own walk sees (the whole tree minus hidden entries and
`node_modules`), which is also the behavior whenever ripgrep cannot be resolved
or an invocation fails — `grep` never fails because ripgrep did.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | File as served rows: `ANCHOR:FILELINE` header + `<anchor>:<line>` markers, or the bare `<anchor>` — that shape is the user's `line_numbers` setting (off by default), no longer a tool parameter, and a call still carrying it is `[E_BAD_SHAPE]`. `offset` takes a 1-based line **or an anchor** (inclusive start; a bare digit string is that number serialized as text and parses as one); `limit` takes a row count **or an anchor** (inclusive end) — with numbering off, the anchor is the only cursor you can see. Every text-mode window ends with one sentence: `[Lines X-Y of N. Omitted K lines. Use read {resume: "TOKEN"} to continue.]` when the body was truncated, otherwise `[Lines X-Y of N. Use offset="ANCHOR" to continue.]` (`offset=N` for a plain line cursor), and `[Lines X-Y of N. End of file.]` at the end of the file. Oversize lines (>200 KB) become a marker + `sed` hint — anchors need full lines. A file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 still reads: decoded lossily (`U+FFFD`), rendered as unserved `[line N] content` rows, not editable — but showing is observing: a lossy read still tells the host the file wa

dsh-hashline-edittool README · `apply_patch` — one change set in one call：`apply_patch` applies one change set in one call: **add**, **update**, **delete** and **move**
across several files. It is the multi-file counterpart of `edit` — single-file anchored
surgery stays `edit`.

A patch is a sequence of **file sections**; every content line is prefixed with `+`, so a
section header is the only thing that can appear un-prefixed:

```text
file src/greet.ts
replace Ab
+  return `hi ${name}`
replace Ef..Gh
section: `apply_patch` — one change set in one call

dsh-hashline-edittool README · `apply_patch` — one change set in one call：Section headers: `file <path>` (update), `new <path>` (create), `move <from> -> <to>`,
`remove <path>` (delete). Hunk headers inside a section: `replace <anchor>` /
`replace <start>..<end>`, `insert <anchor>`, `delete <anchor>` / `delete <start>..<end>`.

The anchor addresses the line — **the patch never copies file content**. The anchors are the
ones from this session's read/grep/diff rows (`Ab`, `Ef`, `Gh`, `Cd`, `Ij` above), so a hunk
can only touch a line the model has actually seen.
section: `apply_patch` — one change set in one call

text:
dsh-hashline-edittool README · `apply_patch` — one change set in one call：Two phases: the **whole patch is checked first** (syntax, shape, paths, anchors) and a rejected
patch changes nothing; then the commit runs **in order and stops at the first failure**,
without rolling back what already landed — re-read the affected files before retrying.
section: `apply_patch` — one change set in one call

text:
dsh-hashline-edittool README · `apply_patch` — one change set in one call：**Every section reuses the single-function tool's own method.** A `new` section goes through
`write`'s create path (the automatic format pass, the language-server notification, and the
anchors for the new file's rows); a `remove` through `delete`'s; a `move` through `rename`'s. The
patch adds only the change set: the whole-patch preflight, the operations in order, and the
stop at the first failure.

**On by default.** `apply_patch.enabled: false` removes the tool and its guidance section.
section: `apply_patch` — one change set in one call

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Output modes：`hashline.output_format` switches the model-facing text between:

- **`text`** (default) — the `ANCHOR:FILELINE` row format shown above;
- **`json`** — pure JSON envelopes (e.g. edit returns `{ ok, path, diff, hints, warnings }`
  where `diff` is a `{"<anchor>": content}` / `{"<anchor>:<line>": content}` dict — the
  key **is** the marker, so its shape follows the same `line_numbers` setting).
  Structured, for models that prefer parsing over row formats.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Output modes：The web cards are unaffected — they render from `presentationMeta`, which is always
structured.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Settings：All keys are the plugin's own **profile configuration** (dsh ≥ 0.1.7): edit them in the web at
**Settings → Plugins → `dsh-hashline-edittool`** — the ROW page's configuration form — and
commit through the page. Every change **hot-reloads**: it takes effect on the next tool
call, no restart. The native-editor view of the same values is the entry's `config:` block in
the profile patch (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`); all keys are optional:

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Settings：```yaml
- id: dsh-hashline-edittool
  config:
    separator: "|"           # marker/content column separator (default ":")
    output_format: text      # "text" | "json"

Migrating from 0.1.6? A pre-0.1.7 `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` is imported **by dsh itself**
during the upgrade. The plugin no longer reads, migrates, or writes any settings file —
the entry configuration on this page is the only source of truth. If an old `hashline:`
key did not carry over, set it in the form above.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Per-preset guidance：The `tool:read` / `tool:edit` / `tool:grep` / `tool:undo_last_edit` / `tool:delete` /
`tool:rename` / `tool:apply_patch` guidance sections are plain-markdown override files in the
plugin's shared home, keyed by preset id — see
[`docs/adr/0001`](docs/adr/0001-guidance-override-files.md). Emptying a file resets to the
compiled default; a broken front-matter fence is fast-failed with a warning.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Error Codes：| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[E_ACCESS]` | File exists but is not readable/writable. |
| `[E_ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS]` | The anchor is live on multiple lines (a freed anchor was re-allocated while the model still held the old binding) — refused; re-read. Nothing was written for that file. |
| `[E_ANCHOR_STATE_DUP]` | The file's anchor state has duplicate anchors (corruption). The state is rebuilt; the edit is refused — re-read to get fresh anchors. Nothing was written. |
| `[E_ANCHOR_REALIGN]` | `grep` asked for anchors by file identity (#414), and the store's rows were written for different content: the file must be read and the allocation retried (the tool does that itself; the code is what the kernel answers). |
| `[E_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE]` / `[E_SEARCH_FAILED]` / `[E_SEARCH_OVERFLOW]` | `grep`'s engine (#414): ripgrep is not installed / the search failed / the search's raw output crossed the 20 MB ceiling. There is no second engine; the error says to narrow pattern, path or include. |
| `[E_AST_DISABLED]` / `[E_AST_PATTERN]` / `[E_AST_TOO_LARGE]` | AST capability off for the language / pattern did not parse as one node / file exceeds the

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Store：Anchor identity, served rows, and undo history live in one SQLite store **keyed by the
workspace** being edited:

```
$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-hashline-edittool/<projectKey>/hash-store.sqlite
```

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Store：`<projectKey>` is a human-navigable encoding of the session's live working directory —
the one DSH reports for the session right now, so a session that moved into a worktree
gets its own store — so parallel workspaces never share anchors or undo history. Callers
outside a workspace fall back to the shared-home store. A 7-day TTL prunes served rows;
rebuilt automatically.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Store：The `delete` tool purges a path's four row families (`anchor_meta`, `anchor_lines`, `served` across every session, `undo` at every depth) in one transaction and reports the logical bytes freed. When those bytes actually drop it writes `pending_vacuum`; shutdown runs a synchronous VACUUM and clears the marker only on success.

dsh-hashline-edittool README · Store：The `rename` tool moves a path's four row families to the new path in one transaction: the destination's residue is purged first, then each family is copied with `INSERT … SELECT` and the old rows deleted — never `UPDATE … SET path`, because the maintained path / row counts are `INSERT` / `DELETE` triggers. Anchors, undo bodies, `served.reported` and `updated_at` move verbatim, so the same anchors stay usable after the rename.

```text
src/
├── index.ts              # entry: mounts tools, settings, LSP, grammar routes
├── config.ts             # settings schema + wiring (hot-reload)
├── tools/                # the 10 tool entry points — thin, no IO of their own
